thread:
Maria (runtime): Heads-up: getting a high-sev from a Dedicated customer hitting big throughput drops on their reserved pool since ~08:10 UTC. They report spikes in token cost and long tail in request queueing despite low avg latency. Screenshot + sample logs attached: https://redwood.internal/acme/esc/3669 :eyes:
Devin (support): ack, can you paste the minimal repro? customer says it started after a config change yesterday.
Maria (runtime): Minimal repro: steady stream of short completion requests (avg 12 tokens) at 350 qps for route /v1/generate. We see many tiny micro-batches and autoscaler oscillating.
Ash (support): customer claim: "we didn't change app, but we rolled a model variant last night". Linking their ticket #ACME-789.
Jordan (sre): looking at node metrics — GPUs are not saturated, but queue depth jumped and worker-level batch sizes are extremely small (median batch_tokens=96, expected ~1024). Autoscaler scaled down nodes at 07:50 then back up at 08:14, so there was a low-concurrency window. Suspect scheduler/pacing mismatch + packer skipping merge. :thinking_face:
Anita (eng-runtime): can you dump scheduler traces? especially continuous-batcher decisions and packer logs. If packer thinks packs are incompatible it won't merge.
Maria (runtime): pasted condensed logs below:
```
[08:09:58] continuous-batcher: accept req id=ri-123 tokens=14 pref=low
[08:09:58] packer: create pack p-9 tgt_tokens=128
[08:09:58] packer: skip_merge p-9 <- p-8 reason=policy_mismatch(fair_weight)
[08:09:58] scheduler: dispatch pack p-9 size=1
[08:09:59] autoscaler: scale_down candidate node=n-5 util=0.12
[08:10:12] continuous-batcher: median_batch_tokens=96 median_items=2
[08:10:14] autoscaler: scale_up node+n-7 reason=queue_latency>150ms
```
Devin (support): interesting line: reason=policy_mismatch(fair_weight). Customer uses per-tenant fairness and we recently changed default "pack_compat_threshold" in the policy ingestion PR. Could be related.
Jordan (sre): also see repeated warning in runtime: "max_batch_tokens < model.quant_window -> degrading packing efficiency". Which model variant did they roll to?
Maria (runtime): they moved from rwd-1.3b-q8 to rwd-1.3b-q4 yesterday evening (rollback attempted earlier today). Model config shows max_batch_tokens=256 on q4 variant while our routing assumes 2048 for that workload.
Anita (eng-runtime): that mismatch explains tiny packs. When max_batch_tokens is low the packer creates many small packs and continuous-batcher can't merge because token ceilings differ. Combined with tenant fair weights it's not merging across tenants.
Devin (support): action items for now from support: request customer to temporarily pin to previous variant (rwd-1.3b-q8) while we triage. They need a rollback guide.
Maria (runtime): repro curl to simulate customer pattern: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.company/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD" -d '{"model":"rwd-1.3b-q4","prompt":"short","max_tokens":16}' &
# run ~350 qps for 2m
```
Ash (support): sent rollback steps to customer, they can do a pinned-route change. Waiting on confirmation. :thumbsup:
Jordan (sre): short-term mitigation we can flip in fleet: increase pack_compat_threshold and allow cross-tenant pack merges when fair_weight delta <= 0.1. Also raise autoscaler min_nodes for that dedicated pool to avoid scale-down during transient tiny-batch windows.
Anita (eng-runtime): logging + telemetry improvements: emit "pack_merge_attempt" metric with cause for skip, and a histogram of resulting pack_token_sizes. That will help detect drift earlier.
Ops-Liu (infra): I'll hold a zoom for a live deploy if we agree on config. Can we schedule a quick canary?
Maria (runtime): proposed steps: 1) Customer rollback to q8 variant (support-led immediate) 2) infra: temporarily raise min_nodes=3 for pool acme-dedicated 3) runtime: enable cross-tenant pack merge throttle (config: pack_compat_threshold -> 0.12) on canary subset 4) add pack_merge_attempt metric and a scheduler trace flag. Anyone object?
Devin (support): no objections, proceed. I'll coordinate with customer.
Jordan (sre): I'll prepare a small runtime patch and a docs blurb on model-variant max_batch_tokens expectations.
Anita (eng-runtime): canary patch contents for ops: 
```
runtime.conf:
  pack_compat_threshold: 0.12
  allow_cross_tenant_merge: true
  scheduler:
    min_pack_items: 1
    max_batch_tokens_override: 2048
```
Jordan (sre): note: max_batch_tokens_override here is a temporary safety net for older routes until model metadata ingestion is fixed.
DeployBot: started canary deployment to pool acme-dedicated-canary-2 at 08:45 UTC.
Ops-Liu (infra): canary up, traffic green. Observing median_batch_tokens increasing to ~900 within 60s.
Maria (runtime): customer confirms rollback in progress. They report immediate throughput improvement after rollback. 
Ash (support): Customer grateful, but asked for a postmortem and permanent fix.
Anita (eng-runtime): agreed — next steps: (A) fix model variant metadata ingestion to ensure max_batch_tokens is correct for q4 variants (B) add scheduler guardrail to avoid autoscale scale-down during sustained small-batch windows (C) telemetry + alert for pack_merge_rate drop.
Jordan (sre): I'll write a short postmortem draft and link the PRs.
Devin (support): closing loop with ACME and creating a ticket to track the permanent fixes.
Maria (runtime): thanks everyone. tagging for follow-ups: @Jordan (sre) @Anita (eng-runtime) @Ops-Liu (infra) :white_check_mark:
